name: SAPPHIRES
full_name: Search for Axion-like Particles via optical Parametric effects with High-Intensity laseRs in Empty Space
summary: An international laser-collision search producing and stimulating the decay of light scalars or pseudoscalars with two-color lasers; it is distinct from the Hefei spin experiment SAPPHIRE.
detection_principle: Focused creation-beam photons undergo quasi-parallel collisions; a second inducing laser stimulates possible resonant ALP decay, with frequency-shifted photons sought.

sites.name: Kyoto University Institute for Chemical Research laser facility, Uji
sites.location: Kyoto University Institute for Chemical Research laser facility, Uji

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified

timeline.event: Search for sub-eV axion-like resonance states via stimulated quasi-parallel laser collisions with the parameterization including fully asymmetric collisional geometry

collaboration.name: SAPPHIRES Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No significant scattering signal; 95% confidence limits on scalar and pseudoscalar mass–coupling parameters were obtained.

science_scope: Produces and detects axions or dark-sector particles in the laboratory, rather than directly measuring Galactic-halo dark-matter flux. It tests interactions of dark-matter candidates; identifying a discovered particle as dark matter would also require establishing its cosmic abundance.
